# Pony AI’s Playbook for Scaling Robotaxis Worldwide

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-11-04T07:44:04.000Z

---

View this post on the web at https://avmarketstrategist.substack.com/p/pony-ais-playbook-for-scaling-robotaxis

Pony AI CEO James Peng on the robotaxi math behind his company: what one car has to earn, who should own it, and how many it takes before the whole company pays for itself.
Dr. James Peng co-founded Pony AI in Silicon Valley in 2016 after years at Google and Baidu. Today the company is listed on Nasdaq and in Hong Kong and plans to run more than 3,500 robotaxis by the end of 2026. I asked him how that fleet is meant to make money.
The numbers come first: what Pony AI counts in its unit economics and what it leaves out, why more and more vehicles belong to partners like Toyota or Verne, how its per-mile cost compares with Waymo’s, and the fleet size at which the company turns cash-flow positive.
Then the map: Zagreb, the planned tests in London and Manchester, Luxembourg with Bolt and Stellantis, Dubai and Doha, and why Peng thinks Germany’s 2021 law needs a smaller first step. It closes with the question investors keep asking: does the virtual driver become a commodity once Uber works with everyone?
